title: doubling counter rotates the two tetrahedra — a machine-checked theorem of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit
description:
doubling counter rotates the two tetrahedra, declared in src/proof/merkaba.lean and accepted by the Lean 4 kernel, sorry-free and axiom-free, closing by by decide.

Statement (Lean):

(dbl tetA).eraseDups.length = 3 ∧ (dbl tetA).all (fun d => tetB.contains d) ∧ (dbl tetB).eraseDups.length = 3 ∧ (dbl tetB).all (fun d => tetA.contains d)

Statement (LaTeX):

\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetA}\right)\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetA}\right),\; d \in \mathrm{tetB} \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetB}\right)\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetB}\right),\; d \in \mathrm{tetA}

What this record establishes. A dated, public, citable deposit of this declaration and its proof, recomputable from the source it names. That is priority. It is not a claim that the result is unknown to the literature: prior art for this file is recorded in src/proof/priorart.lean as unclassified — no prior-art search has been performed, so no novelty is asserted.

Scope. The declaration is decided over a finite domain by exhaustion. It settles no Clay Millennium Problem and claims no quantum speedup. 0/7.
